name: Put Ratio Backspread 1x3
summary: Sell one nearer put and buy three further-OTM puts; maximum crash convexity per dollar, with a deep defined valley. Obscure, theta-heavy, and usually inferior to the 1x2 except as an explicit tail hedge.

legs.strike_rule: Short put ATM, 0.50 delta. Covered by one of the three long puts.
Three long puts at 0.10-0.20 delta, placed so the package opens near zero cost.

max_profit: very large below the long strike -- payoff slope is 2x a 1x2 backspread
max_loss: (short strike - long strike) * 100 - net credit (or + debit), at the long strike at expiry. Defined.
breakevens: upper: short strike - credit per share; lower: long strike - max loss per share, reached quickly given three long puts

greeks.gamma: strongly positive below the long strike
greeks.vega: strongly positive -- the largest positive vega per dollar of any Level 3 structure in this family

when_to_use: As a portfolio tail hedge rather than a standalone trade: it pays enormously in a >15% drawdown and costs little if opened for a credit. Put skew makes credit entries rare, so check pricing before committing. Otherwise prefer the 1x2.
entry_rules: MARKED AS SPECIALIST -- default to the 1x2 put backspread unless this is explicitly a tail hedge.
IV rank <= 20 AND 10-delta put IV minus ATM IV <= 10 vol points (otherwise the three long wings are prohibitively expensive).
Short put delta ~0.50; long puts delta 0.10-0.20.
Ratio exactly 1:3 (GCD 1). The short put is covered by one of the three long puts inside the same MLeg order -- Level 3 submittable.
Package must open for a net credit or a debit <= 5% of (short strike - long strike).
OI >= 1000 on the long strike, quoted size >= 30.
If used as a portfolio hedge, size the number of units so that a 20% index decline produces a gain of roughly 10-15% of equity, and accept the valley cost as an insurance premium.
management_rules: Take profit at 2.5x the max-loss amount, or on a 2.0 ATR move below the long strike.
Vol harvest: if IV rank rises above 60 with price roughly unchanged, close and re-establish further out -- vega gains are the most reliable payoff this structure produces.
Valley stop: at 45 DTE, if the underlying sits within 2% of the long strike, close.
If net delta is beyond -1.50 per unit, sell one long put, converting to a 1x2.
As a standing hedge, roll to a new 60-90 DTE expiry every 30 days rather than letting the current one decay.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: short put ITM at 15:30 ET on expiry day -> close the whole package immediately; assignment would deliver 100 shares per unit.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: short put ITM with extrinsic < $0.10 on any day -> close that session.
assignment_risk: Single short put, covered by one of the three long puts. Bounded economically; operationally it would deliver 100 long shares per unit during a market decline, which the account cannot fund. The ATM short strike means this guard fires often -- it must be automated.
buying_power: Width of the covering vertical: (short strike - long strike)*100 - credit per unit.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 1000 and size >= 30 on the deep wing; on anything but SPY/QQQ/IWM these strikes will not support a 3-lot package.
common_mistakes: Buying it when skew is already steep (paying up for the hedge exactly when everyone else is); letting it decay rather than rolling at 30 DTE; sizing it like a directional trade instead of insurance.
zero_dte_notes: Not usable. A tail hedge with no time is not a hedge.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
